Lemma
[Forward difference quotient of the maximum of a compact family]

↗ def:forward-difference-quotient ↗ lem:max-function-continuous-product

Let $X$ be nonempty and compact, let $t_0<b$, and let $F,F'$ be continuous on $X\times \Ar $, with $\partial _sF(x,s)=F'(x,s)$ for $s\in (t_0,b)$. If $F'(x,t_0)\le c$ at every maximizer of $F(\cdot ,t_0)$, then the forward difference quotient of $F_{\max }$ at $t_0$ is at most $c$.
Proof

\sketch

↗ lem:max-function-continuous-product Otherwise some $r>c$ and times $z\downarrow t_0$ have maximum difference quotient at least $r$. Choose maximizers $x_z$ at time $z$. The mean value theorem produces $s_z\in (t_0,z)$ with $F'(x_z,s_z)\ge r$. Compactness gives a cluster point $x_0$, and continuity makes $x_0$ a maximizer at $t_0$ with $F'(x_0,t_0)\ge r>c$, a contradiction.

□
